main_claim: Better connectivity may support enterprise activity by lowering information, communication, coordination and market-access costs
theoretical_rationale: Economically stronger provinces may attract operator investment
distinct_predictions: Enterprise growth precedes rather than follows connectivity improvement
variables_required: Lagged enterprise outcomes; operator investment timing; connectivity leads
discriminating_test: Compare temporal ordering with preregistered leads and lags in a future associational design
elimination_evidence: Credible predetermined rollout variation plus absence of enterprise-leading patterns across verified measures

distinct_predictions: Both measures move with independently measured local development shocks
variables_required: Predetermined infrastructure; urbanization; FDI; income; governance
discriminating_test: Add preregistered verified shock measures and negative controls in a future design

main_claim: Better connectivity may support enterprise activity by lowering information, communication, coordination and market-access costs
theoretical_rationale: Changing users, devices, providers or test locations may change measured speed without equivalent infrastructure change
distinct_predictions: VNNIC changes track test composition or disagree with an independent measurement source
discriminating_test: Compare VNNIC with a bounded Ookla validation pilot and composition diagnostics
elimination_evidence: Concordant changes across independent measures plus stable composition diagnostics
new_evidence: Four fixed-Q2 Ookla partitions provide 63-province coverage; direction and dispersion mostly agree but annual ranks are weak/inconsistent

remaining_limitation: Both sources rely on voluntary speed-test participation; test/device/provider composition remains incomplete

main_claim: Better connectivity may support enterprise activity by lowering information, communication, coordination and market-access costs
theoretical_rationale: Higher registered enterprise density may reflect formalization or relocation rather than new real activity
